findings.title: Sender validation is bypassed when the Integration row does not exist yet
findings.body: GitHubInstallation only compares github_authenticated_user with the installer when an Integration row already exists. If Integration.objects.get raises DoesNotExist it immediately calls pipeline.next_step(), which proceeds to create and link the integration. The Integration row is normally created by GitHub's asynchronous installation webhook, and GitHub provides no ordering guarantee between that webhook and the browser redirect/OAuth pipeline. A user whose GitHub login differs from the installer can therefore claim the installation if they reach this step before the webhook is processed, or if the webhook is delayed or missed, defeating the validation added by this PR.

findings.title: Missing sender metadata causes a KeyError instead of the installation error page
findings.body: The new check directly indexes integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]. Integrations created before sender metadata was recorded, or created through paths where no sender was stored, do not have this key. If such an ACTIVE integration remains after its OrganizationIntegration is removed and someone attempts to install it again, this line raises KeyError/TypeError and returns a 500 instead of either proceeding safely or showing the intended invalid-installation page. The metadata should be read defensively and a missing sender handled explicitly.

findings.title: GitHub token-exchange and user-info failures are not converted to the installation error page
findings.body: safe_urlopen at line 423 is called outside the try block, and get_user_info at line 434 is also unguarded. Network failures, GitHub HTTP errors, or an invalid/unusable access token can therefore raise out of OAuthLoginView.dispatch and produce a 500. This contradicts the PR's stated behavior that failures to obtain a valid access token or verify the GitHub user should show the invalid-installation error page.

findings.title: Installation now depends on separate GitHub login OAuth credentials
findings.body: OAuthLoginView uses GitHubIdentityProvider.get_oauth_client_id/get_oauth_client_secret, which are the github-login.* credentials for GitHub SSO, not the github-app.client-id/github-app.client-secret credentials used to configure the GitHub App integration. Deployments that configured only the GitHub App, as previously sufficient for installing this integration, will now redirect to GitHub with an empty or invalid client_id and cannot complete installation at all. The flow should use the GitHub App's OAuth credentials or otherwise not make GitHub login configuration a new prerequisite.

findings.title: test_installation_not_found no longer exercises the installation-not-found path
findings.body: The test replaces the GitHub installation endpoint with a 404, but its second setup request supplies a state value that does not match the pipeline signature, so OAuthLoginView returns the generic invalid-installation page before build_integration can call the installation endpoint. The 404 stub is therefore never meaningfully exercised and the assertion would pass even if the installation-not-found handling regressed; the test needs a valid OAuth state/code exchange before asserting the 404 behavior.
